## About
CARspec is an independent Toyota, Lexus and Scion maintenance and repair shop on Corporate Way in Eden Prairie. After years of experience working for the dealerships, owner John Cleveland set out to build a new kind of shop: one that offers a competitive price point, technical prowess, honesty and environmentally friendly practices in a clean, transparent environment.
Our technicians are formerly factory trained and hybrid certified, and we use and install genuine Toyota, Lexus and Scion repair parts. We handle the maintenance and repair needs of conventional, hybrid and full electric vehicles in a state of the art, low environmental impact shop.
We serve Bloomington, Eastern Carver County, Chanhassen, Chaska, Deephaven, Eden Prairie, Edina, Excelsior, Golden Valley, Hopkins, Minnetonka, Plymouth, Richfield, Savage, St. Louis Park, Shakopee, Victoria and Wayzata. Customers rate us 4.9 from 253 Google reviews.

## Services
- Oil changes: Routine oil service for Toyota, Lexus and Scion vehicles.
- Tire rotation, repair and replacement: Rotation, repair and new tires when it's time.
- Brake service and replacement: Brake inspection, service and replacement.
- Timing belt replacement: Timing belt replacement for engines that use one.
- Factory recommended maintenance: The maintenance your vehicle's maker recommends, done by technicians who know these cars.
- Transmission, coolant, differential, transfer case and brake fluid replacement: Fluid service across the drivetrain, cooling system and brakes.
- Hybrid Synergy Drive diagnostics and repair: Diagnosis and repair of Toyota's hybrid drive system.
- Hybrid battery diagnostics and replacement: Testing and replacement of hybrid batteries.

## FAQ
Q: Are you a Toyota or Lexus dealership?
A: No. CARspec is an independently owned and operated shop, not affiliated with Toyota Motor Corp and not a factory-authorized repair facility.

Q: Do you work on hybrids and electric vehicles?
A: Yes. We service conventional, hybrid and full electric Toyota, Lexus and Scion vehicles.

Q: Are you taking new customers?
A: Not always. We balance how much work we take in so current customers get good service. Call and ask when we're accepting new customers.

Q: How do I get an estimate or make an appointment?
A: Give us a call. We're open Monday through Friday, 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM, and closed Saturday and Sunday.

## What customers say
- "I decided to do a Google search for a Toyota specialty shop in Minnesota and stumbled upon CARspec. I read the reviews before attempting to contact the shop. I did this research toward the end of 2025. I did read in the reviews that people were unable to make an appointment with CARspec. And John (owner) replied with an explanation to why that is the case. And, to me, that is totally understandable - the demand for their services is off the charts. I continued to read more reviews and stumbled upon another of John's responses, where he stated they would be opening up to new customers soon. That was a big relief, so I called CARspec and John answered. John is a professional and honest individual. I felt confident in John, just simply talking to him over the phone. I asked if they are currently accepting new customers and he let me know that they weren't currently accepting new customers, however, would be accepting new customers starting February 2026. I accepted the answer and told him I would call back again when Feb 2026 came around.

Fast forward to Feb 3, 2026, I gave John a call. Asked if they were accepting new customers and John said yes and that Feb is almost completely booked. He said that the next available slot would be Feb 24/25 (can't remember exact date). I called on Feb 3, and the next availability was the end of February. In only 3 days, their Feb schedule almost completely booked up. Thank goodness I called when I did.

I scheduled a time for John and his team to inspect my 2006 Camry. After inspection, John said the car has served its purpose and lived a good life and recommended to move onto a new car. It has 240,000+ miles and is 20 years old. So, understandable.

Next up, I brought my 2017 Highlander to John and his team. Told me the car is looking good overall. Only recommendations were new spark plugs, transfer case fluid change, and differential fluid change. John let me know that for this job, it would probably be completed by Monday (since the inspection appointment was Friday morning, and inspection completed around 12pm-1pm, and they close at 5pm). I decided to schedule a different date for the job. They are so busy that when I scheduled a different date for the work to be done, it was almost a month out.

Fast forward a month, I bring in my Highlander and John and his team took care of my Highlander. I was expecting to notice a bit of performance enhancement, but didn't feel much different, but John did say it was already in good shape. So, not really a surprise there. The work done was really just maintenance for the car to keep working as good as it should.

Went to pick up the Highlander and the grand total cost was right around where John quoted me, maybe even a bit cheaper. To have the meticulous work done by John and his team without being rushed like how technicians at dealerships are rushed, I'll pay for that Peace of mind anyday. But honestly, I think their prices might be better than at dealerships. I'm not 100% sure because I know that I don't want to take my cars to the dealerships, so i just took it to CARspec first, especially since their "bad" reviews aren't actually bad things about their customer service or quality of work - it's that they don't have enough resources to meet the demand for their services. 😄

Anyways. If you want to get your car checked out by John and his team, just call in and ask when they'd be accepting new customers. You won't regret waiting for John and his team to have some availability.

P.s. John offered my kids some free legos. What an awesome owner!

tldr: Great auto shop for maintenance work on your Toyotas (Lexus/Scion are Toyotas). Just make sure you call in first to see if they are currently accepting new customers. If they aren't, hopefully you only need to wait a month or two before their schedule opens up to new customers.

Thanks again, John!" (Tong Yang, 5/5)
